fast.meaning: Quickly. In some places in this book it means 'held firmly' or 'deeply'.
fast.whyHard: This word has more than one meaning.

anchors.context: the Queen went so fast that it was all she could do

senses.meaning: Held firmly, so that it cannot move or come out. Here the oars are stuck in the water.

anchors.context: every now and then the oars got fast in it
which made the oars stick fast in the water
the blade of one of the oars got fast in the water

senses.meaning: Deeply. It is used to say that someone is sleeping very well.

anchors.context: both Queens were fast asleep, and snoring loud

guard.meaning: On a train, the man who checks who has paid.
guard.whyHard: This word has more than one meaning.

senses.meaning: On a train, the man who checks who has paid.

anchors.context: “Tickets, please!” said the guard, putting his head in at the window

senses.meaning: To keep safe from something bad. "Guard against" means to keep safe from.

anchors.context: “To guard against the bites of sharks,” the Knight replied
